Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

sort of adverb and phrase

also kind of, a sort of, a kind of, as it were, in a way, so to speak

classical

Cic. Fin. 5.43: in puerīs virtūtum quasi scintillās vidēmus
Cic. Off. 1.54: quasi sēminārium reī pūblicae
Cic. Att. 5.2.2: quasi pusillam Rōmam

quasi

adverb, before the word it softens · Wiktionary

as it were, a sort of, so to speak

Cicero’s way of excusing a bold word or a metaphor, often with quīdam: quasi ferream quandam, “a sort of iron (virtue)” (Amic. 48, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • quīdam, quaedam, quoddam — a sort of, a kind of; a certain

    pronoun and adjective, after the word it softens · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.10: timiditāte quādam ingenuā (Lewis & Short); Gell. praef. 2: quasi quoddam litterārum penus · Wiktionary

  • quōdam modō — in a way, in a sense, sort of

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.5.5: est mīrō quōdam modō adfectus

Examples

  • in puerīs virtūtum quasi scintillās vidēmus

    in children we see sparks, as it were, of the virtuesCic. Fin. 5.43

  • eaque mihi ad subsidium memoriae quasi quoddam litterārum penus recondēbam

    and I stored them away as a sort of larder of letters, to help my memoryGell. praef. 2

  • est mīrō quōdam modō adfectus

    he is in a strange sort of moodCic. Att. 1.5.5

See also kind, quite.
